judgment.rationale: The latest reports supply the requested discriminator: Win-key shortcuts fail while Grab And Move uses the Windows modifier, and toggling Grab And Move restores them. This directly matches the open canonical Grab And Move tracker #47585.
evidence: The original report describes Win+A to Win+N failing outside Explorer/Desktop.
The author says the issue reproduces in 0.100.2 with Grab And Move's modifier set to Windows and temporarily recovers after toggling Grab And Move.
Another reporter confirms Win+O fails in 0.101.2373 while Grab And Move is enabled.
Issue #47585 is open for Grab And Move Win-key interference with other Win-key hotkeys and contains the same Keyboard Manager reproduction.
Current Grab And Move KeyboardProc absorbs Win keydown and replays it when no drag occurs, a shared input boundary that can affect other Win-key consumers.
judgment.recommended_action: Consolidate this confirmed duplicate into #47585; do not open a separate Keyboard Manager fix design.

fix_assessment.rationale: The canonical open issue #47585 owns the same Grab And Move Windows-modifier interception path.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager and other Win-key shortcuts fail inconsistently when Grab And Move is configured to activate with the Windows key, matching the active shared Grab And Move tracker.
known_information: The author identified Windows as Grab And Move's modifier and confirmed a toggle workaround.
A current prerelease user reproduces a Win+O failure under the same utility configuration.
The issue timeline cross-references closed #47891, while #47585 remains open.
Grab And Move tracks absorbed Win state and replays the key when no drag occurs.
inferences: Hook state or replay ordering in the Grab And Move Win-key path can affect multiple hotkey consumers, but #47760 does not establish a Keyboard Manager-specific defect.
issue_context.analysis: The current source and latest issue comments support a shared input-hook classification. Consolidating preserves the decisive reproduction data in the canonical tracker and prevents fragmented fixes.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue and all eight comments.
Inspected src/modules/GrabAndMove/GrabAndMove/main.cpp KeyboardProc, including Win absorption/replay behavior.
Reviewed focused Grab And Move history, including Win key replay fixes.
Searched related live reports and found #47585 as the direct active match.

actions.label: Link canonical Grab And Move tracker

comment.body: Thanks for confirming that this reproduces with Grab And Move enabled using the Windows-key modifier and temporarily recovers when Grab And Move is toggled. That is the distinguishing behavior already tracked in #47585: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/47585. The same Win-key interception path can affect Keyboard Manager and other Win-key hotkeys, so please add any further current-build reproduction details to #47585 to keep the fix investigation consolidated.
